## Verdicts on Schema-Flagged Findings

**MERGE C0004 <- C0001** — Same root cause: unanchored `re.search` matching gate statuses anywhere in block text. CC2_F001 and Codex_F001 describe the identical mechanism (line 111 `re.search` without line anchoring). Withdrawing CC2_F001 as duplicate.

**DIFFERENTIATE C0005 from C0001** — CC2_F002 (C0005) is about the *header marker regex* at line 58–62 (colon placement relative to parenthetical group), NOT about gate-status matching within the block. Different line, different mechanism, different consequence:
- C0001: gate status matched at wrong position *inside* an already-extracted block → wrong PASS/FAIL verdict
- C0005: header marker regex fails to match certain valid header formats → entire block missed → all gates reported as FAIL (false negatives)

These are independent parsers operating on different parts of the input. Cosine similarity reflects shared vocabulary ("regex", "ADMISSIBILITY", "match") not shared mechanism.

---

**CONFIRM C0001** — Verified: `re.search` at line 111 scans the entire `block` string. A gate name appearing in another gate's explanatory parenthetical (e.g., `d_tool: PASS (verified S_min threshold)`) would cause `S_min` to false-match at that position. Fix proposed (line-anchored matching) is correct in direction.

**CONFIRM C0003** — Verified: `σ_measured: N/A` is treated as passing unconditionally (line 119–120). When the finding text contains a `<<<< SEARCH` block (indicating a proposed fix exists), N/A is semantically wrong — §15 requires post-fix measurement. The parser cannot enforce this alone but should not accept N/A when fix evidence is present.

---

## New Finding

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.55
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.35
FIND: The section_terminator regex (line 80–85) uses only `re.MULTILINE` while the marker_match regex (line 58–61) uses `re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE`. This means the parser accepts case-insensitive ADMISSIBILITY headers (e.g., `admissibility:`, `Admissibility:`) but requires EXACTLY uppercase section terminators. If a model writes `Novelty:` or `novelty:` as its next section header, the terminator won't fire and the extracted block will consume all subsequent text until end-of-string or the next uppercase header.
FOLLOW: When the terminator fails, the `block` variable contains everything from the ADMISSIBILITY header to end-of-string. Gate-matching then scans this over-large block. Combined with the unanchored matching issue (C0001), text from NOVELTY, CORROBORATION, or other downstream sections could contain gate names adjacent to PASS/FAIL tokens, producing false-pass results (gates incorrectly marked as passing when they were actually unreported). The consequence is silent data corruption in the feedback channel — a model that failed ADMISSIBILITY might not receive the corrective feedback it needs.
ANALYSE: SOFT constraint. The CDSFL protocol mandates all-caps section headers, so well-formed model output won't trigger this. However, the parser's docstring explicitly claims "case-insensitive" and "forgiving" behaviour — accepting case-insensitive input at the header but not at the terminator is an internal consistency violation. CONFIRMED as a logic defect (inconsistent case handling between entry and exit of the same parser).
